schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE PID IN (SELECT DISTINCT I1.PID FROM INSURANCE I1 JOIN INSURANCE I2 ON I1.PID != I2.PID AND I1.TIV_2015 = I2.TIV_2015) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) AS TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE PID IN (SELECT DISTINCT I1.PID FROM INSURANCE I1 JOIN INSURANCE I2 ON I1.PID != I2.PID AND I1.TIV_2015 = I2.TIV_2015) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 1000, 1500, 34.0522, -118.2437); INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (2, 1000, 1200, 34.0522, -118.2437);
explanation: Q1 filters policies that have the same TIV_2015 value as at least one other policy AND unique latitude and longitude. Q2 filters policies that have the same TIV_2015 value as at least one other policy AND unique latitude and longitude, but uses a different method to identify such policies.
counterexample_dsp: A policy with TIV_2015 = 1000 and unique latitude/longitude, and another policy with TIV_2015 = 1000 and the same latitude/longitude as the first policy.
